niche: a provincial statistics bureau's regional payroll-jobs series, built from the revenue service's monthly employer returns and seasonally adjusted for a statutory rapid-response trigger, across the January 2026 change that brought the quarterly remitters into the monthly returns
stakeholder_role: manager of the bureau's regional labour statistics unit

spine.entity: one municipality's payroll jobs in one industry in one month
spine.source: synthetic (constructed in the layout of a tax authority's monthly employer-return statistics)

world.geography: Canada (an unnamed province; fictional economic regions)
invented_names: Bureau of Statistics and Economic Analysis

driver: The decisive quantity compares two periods that both lie after a documented change in what the source counts, so the change looks irrelevant, but the seasonal pattern used to adjust them is estimated from history spanning it, and an adjustment that does not first remove the change as a level shift lets it leak into the seasonal factors and moves the latest period most where the change was largest.
driver_concrete: Each region's first-quarter 2027 seasonally adjusted payroll jobs are set against its 2026 average, both on the coverage the returns have had since the quarterly remitters joined the monthly returns in January 2026; a default seasonal adjustment estimates the seasonal pattern across that step, inflating the first-quarter factors and pulling the latest quarter down where the remitters hold the most jobs, while official practice removes the step as a level shift in the regARIMA pre-adjustment (or restates the earlier history) before the seasonal filters run.
stump: The default path designates Brennick Valley, Kestrow North, Oslin Shore and Pellmarsh Hills because step 4 estimates each region's seasonal pattern across the January 2026 coverage step without removing it: the step inflates the first-quarter seasonal factors in proportion to its size, which pulls the first quarter of 2027 below the line in Kestrow North and Oslin Shore, where the quarterly remitters hold over a fifth of the jobs; removing the step as a level shift before the seasonal pattern is estimated (or restating the earlier history to the new coverage) designates Brennick Valley and Pellmarsh Hills only.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms the returns, reads the January 2026 coverage note correctly (both compared periods are on the new coverage) and seasonally adjusts each region's whole series with STL or the classical moving-average method designates Brennick Valley, Kestrow North, Oslin Shore and Pellmarsh Hills, against Brennick Valley and Pellmarsh Hills.
domain_test: Official time-series production pre-adjusts a documented break in an administrative source as a level shift in the regARIMA model before the seasonal filters (the client's survey-research-official-statistics seasonal-adjustment pattern 1); the quantity is an official seasonally adjusted series a statute reads, built from a return whose coverage a filing rule changed, and outside official series production neither the coverage rule nor the statutory series exists.

differentiation.task139: task139 reads an intake-randomised intervention's effect per assigned unit rather than per recorded case (a causal estimand); task453 removes a documented coverage step as a level shift before estimating seasonal factors (official time-series production), with no intervention and no assignment
differentiation.task30: task30 round 3 segmented a calibration corpus to its post-change cohort; task453's post-change span (15 months) is too short to estimate a seasonal pattern, so the full history is kept and the change removed as a level shift, and segmenting to the post-change months is one of its wrong rungs

notes: Drawn 2026-10-13. Prototype in scratch (t453/proto3 to proto6, statsmodels in a scratch venv): default STL and the classical moving-average decomposition designate the high-step regions in every seed; robust STL lands the golden when the irregular is small (it down-weights the months around the step) and misses at a realistic regional irregular of 0.6 to 1.0 per cent; every step-aware method (regression with a level shift over three windows, STL and the classical method on the restated history, pre-break factors) designates the same regions.
